translations.text: The Lord called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting, saying:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the Lord, you shall bring your offerings from the livestock, either from the herd or from the flock.

If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall offer a male without blemish. He shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting and offer it so that he may be accepted before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and it will be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.
He shall slaughter the young bull before the Lord. The priests, Aaron’s sons, shall present the blood and splash it all around the altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall skin the animal for the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
The priests, Aaron’s sons, shall put fire on the altar and pile wood on the fire.
The priests, Aaron’s sons, shall arrange the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood on the fire on the altar.
He shall wash its entrails and legs with water, and the priest shall offer all of it up on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his offering is from the flock, from the sheep or the goats, as a burnt offering, he shall offer a male without blemish.
He shall slaughter it beside the altar on its north side before the Lord. The priests, Aaron’s sons, shall splash its blood all around the altar.
He shall cut it into pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest shall arrange them on the wood on the fire on the altar.
He shall wash its entrails and legs with water. The priest shall present all of it and offer it up on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his offering to the Lord is a burnt offering of birds, he shall bring his offering to the Lord from the turtledoves or the young pigeons.
The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and offer it up on the altar. Its blood shall be drained out against the side of the altar all around.
He shall remove its crop with the food in it and throw it beside the altar on the east side, in the place for the ashes.

He shall split it open between its wings without separating it. The priest shall offer it up on the altar, on the wood on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
When someone brings a grain offering to the Lord, his offering shall be fine flour. He shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.

He shall bring it to the priest, a son of Aaron, who shall take from it a handful of the fine flour and oil, together with all the frankincense. The priest shall offer its memorial portion up on the altar, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy portion of the Lord’s offerings.
When you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be of fine flour: unleavened cakes mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers mixed with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it shall be unleavened fine flour mixed with oil.
Break it into pieces and pour oil over it. It is [?] fine flour.
If your offering is a grain offering prepared in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall bring to the Lord the grain offering prepared in any of these ways. You shall present it to the priest, and he shall offer it up on the altar to the Lord.
The priest shall set aside the memorial portion from the grain offering and offer it up on the altar, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons, a most holy portion of the Lord’s offerings.
No offering of fine flour that you present to the Lord shall be made with leaven, for you shall not offer up any leaven or honey as an offering to the Lord.
You may present them to the Lord as offerings of firstfruits, but they shall not be offered up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
You shall season every offering of your fine flour with salt. You shall not leave the salt of your God's covenant out of your fine flour. With every offering of yours you shall present salt.
If you present an offering of firstfruits to the Lord, you shall present ears of grain roasted in fire, crushed and cleaned grain, as your firstfruits offering.
You shall put oil and frankincense on it. It is an offering.
The priest shall offer up its memorial portion from the crushed grain and the oil, together with all the frankincense, as an offering to the Lord.
If his offering is a sacrifice of well-being, and he presents it from the cattle, he shall present a male or female without blemish before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting. The priests, Aaron's sons, shall splash the blood against all sides of the altar.
From the sacrifice of well-being he shall present an offering to the Lord: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them at the flanks. He shall remove the lobe of the liver along with the kidneys.
The priests, Aaron's sons, shall offer it up on the altar, on the burnt offering and on the wood that is on the fire, as an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his offering is from the flock, as a burnt sacrifice to the Lord, he shall present a male or female without blemish.
If he presents his offering from the lambs, he shall present it before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it before the Lord at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Aaron's sons shall splash its blood against all sides of the altar.

From the burnt sacrifice he shall present an offering to the Lord: its fat and its entire fat tail, which he shall remove close to its loins, and the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them at the flanks. He shall remove the lobe of the liver along with the kidneys.
The priest shall offer it up on the altar as food, an offering to the Lord.
If his offering is a burnt offering from the goats, he shall present it before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on its head and slaughter it before the tent of meeting. Aaron's sons shall splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
From it he shall present his offering, an offering to the Lord: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails.
And the two kidneys and the fat on them, which is on the flanks, and the lobe of the liver with the kidneys, he shall [?].
The priest shall offer them up on the altar as food, an offering with a pleasing aroma. All fat belongs to the Lord.
This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations, wherever you live: you shall eat neither fat nor blood.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When anyone sins unintentionally by doing any of the things that the Lord's commandments forbid,
if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt upon the people, he shall present to the Lord a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
He must bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord. He must lay his hand on the bull’s head and slaughter the bull before the Lord.
The anointed priest must take some of the bull’s blood and bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the Lord, in front of the curtain of the sanctuary.

The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before the Lord in the tent of meeting. He shall pour out all the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
He must remove all the fat of the bull offered as a sin offering: the fat covering the internal organs and all the fat on the internal organs.
He must prepare the two kidneys and the fat on them near the flanks, and the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys.
Just as it is removed from the bull sacrificed as a burnt offering, the priest must offer these up on the altar of burnt offering.
The bull’s hide and all its flesh, together with its dung, its head, its legs, and its internal organs—
he must take the whole bull outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are dumped, and burn it on wood over a fire. It must be burned where the ashes are dumped.
If the whole congregation of Israel goes astray, and the matter is hidden from the congregation’s eyes, and they do something forbidden by any of the Lord’s commandments and become guilty,
and the sin they have committed becomes known, the whole congregation must present a young bull as a sin offering and bring it before the tent of meeting.
The elders of the congregation must lay their hands on the bull’s head before the Lord, and they must slaughter the bull before the Lord.
The anointed priest must bring some of the bull’s blood to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the curtain.

He must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that stands before the Lord in the tent of meeting. He must pour out all the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall separate all its fat from it and offer it up on the altar.
He must do with this bull as he did with the bull of the sin offering; that is what he must do with it. The priest must make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
He must take the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the congregation’s sin offering.
If a ruler sins and unintentionally does something forbidden by any of the commandments of the Lord his God and becomes guilty,
if the sin he has committed becomes known to him, he must bring as his offering a young male goat without blemish.
He must lay his hand on the young goat’s head and slaughter it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the Lord. It is a sin offering.

The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
He must offer up all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of the burnt offering. The priest must make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
If someone from among the people of the land sins unintentionally and does something forbidden by any of the Lord’s commandments and becomes guilty,
if the sin he has committed becomes known to him, he must bring as his offering a young female goat without blemish for the sin he has committed.
He must lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.

The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and sprinkle it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour out all the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.

He shall remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the sacrifice of the burnt offering. The priest shall burn it on the altar as an offering to the Lord, a pleasing aroma. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
If he brings his sin offering from the lambs, he shall bring a female without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and sprinkle it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.

He shall deal with all its fat as he dealt with the fat of the lamb from the sacrifice of the burnt offering. The priest shall burn it on the altar, on the offerings to the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed, and he will be forgiven.
If a person sins by hearing a call to testify under oath, and he is a witness who has seen or knows something but does not disclose it, he shall bear the guilt of his sin.

Or if a person touches anything unclean—the carcass of an unclean wild animal, the carcass of an unclean domestic animal, or the carcass of an unclean crawling creature—and it escapes his notice, he has become unclean and has sinned.
Or if he touches human uncleanness, any uncleanness by which he may become unclean, and it escapes his notice, but he then realizes it, he has sinned.

Or if a person swears with an utterance of his lips to do harm or to do good, in anything a person declares under oath, and it escapes his notice, but he then realizes it, he has sinned in one of these things.
When he has sinned in one of these things, he shall confess the sin he committed in that matter.
He shall bring his offering to the Lord for the sin he committed: a female from the flock, a ewe or a young female goat, as his sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.
If he cannot afford to bring a ewe, he shall bring as an offering for his sin two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
He shall bring them to the priest, who shall offer the one for the sin offering first. He shall wring its head at the back of its neck but shall not sever it.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the remaining blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
He shall prepare the other as a burnt offering according to its prescribed rule. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed, and he will be forgiven.

If he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring as his offering for the sin he committed a tenth of a seah of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest. The priest shall take a handful of it as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, on the offerings to the Lord. It is a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed in any of these things, and he will be forgiven. It shall belong to the priest, as the fine flour does.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

If a person acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally with regard to the Lord’s holy things, he shall bring his offering to the Lord: a ram without blemish from the flock, valued in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, as an offering.

He shall repay what he has wrongfully taken from the holy things, add a fifth to it, and give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the offering, and he will be forgiven.
If a person sins by doing any of the things that the Lord’s commandments forbid, even though he does not know that he has sinned, he shall bear the guilt of his sin.

He shall bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, of the required value, as an offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the error he committed without knowing it, and he will be forgiven.
It is an offering for sin; he shall bring an offering to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
If a person sins and acts unfaithfully against the Lord by deceiving his neighbor concerning a deposit or a business partnership, or by robbery, or by defrauding his neighbor.
Or if someone finds a lost item and lies about it, and swears falsely about any of the things people do and thereby sin.
When he sins and becomes guilty, he must return what he took by force, what he obtained by fraud, what was entrusted to him, or the lost item he found.
Or whatever he swore falsely about, he must repay its full value and add a fifth to it. He must give it to its owner on the day he brings his offering.
He must bring his offering to the LORD: a ram without defect from the flock, at the assessed value, as a guilt offering to the priest.
The priest will make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for any of the things people do and thereby sin.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:

“Command Aaron and his sons and tell them: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering is to burn on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar must be kept burning on it.
The priest shall put on linen garments and wear linen clothing against his body. He shall remove the ashes left when the fire consumed the burnt offering on the altar and place them beside the altar.
The priest must take off his clothes and put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
The fire shall keep burning on the altar and shall not go out. The priest shall heap wood on it every morning, arrange the burnt offering on it, and offer up the fat of the peace offerings on it.
The fire must be kept burning continually on the altar; it must not go out.
This is the law of the grain offering. Aaron’s sons must present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.

He must take from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering and its oil, together with all the frankincense on the grain offering, and burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma, a memorial portion to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons must eat what remains of it. It must be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they must eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it to them as their share of my offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male among Aaron’s descendants may eat it. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations concerning the LORD’s offerings. Whoever touches them will become holy.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:

“This is the offering of Aaron and his sons that they must present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of a seah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening, continually.
It must be prepared on a griddle with oil. Prepare it [?]. Break the grain offering into pieces, and offer it as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed to succeed him must prepare it. As a lasting ordinance, it must be burned completely to the LORD.
Every grain offering of a priest must be burned completely; it must not be eaten.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:

“Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them: This is the law of the sin offering. The sin offering must be slaughtered before the LORD in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it for purification must eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
Whoever touches its meat will become holy. If any of its blood splashes onto a garment, the garment on which it splashes must be washed in a holy place.
The clay vessel in which it is cooked must be broken. If it is cooked in a bronze vessel, the vessel must be scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among Aaron’s descendants may eat it, because it is most holy.
Any sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the sanctuary must not be eaten; it must be burned in the fire.
This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.
They shall slaughter the guilt offering in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, and they shall sprinkle its blood all around the altar.
He shall present all its fat from it: the fat tail and the fat covering the internal organs.
He shall prepare the two kidneys and their fat, and the lobe of the liver along with the kidneys.
The priest shall offer them up on the altar as an offering to the Lord. It is a sin offering.
Every male among Aaron's sons may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering; you shall have one law for both. It shall belong to the priest who makes atonement with it.
The priest who offers a whole burnt offering for a man's sin shall have the hide of the whole burnt offering that he offers.
Every offering of fine flour baked in an oven, and everything prepared in a pan and on a griddle, shall belong to the priest who offers it.
Every offering of fine flour, whether mixed with oil or dry, shall belong to all Aaron's sons, each receiving his share.
This is the law of the sacrifice of the peace offering presented to the Lord.

If he offers it as a thanksgiving offering, he shall offer with his thanksgiving sacrifice unleavened cakes mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour stirred together [?], cakes mixed with oil.
Along with cakes of leavened bread, he shall present his offering with his thanksgiving sacrifice of peace offerings.
He shall present one of each of these offerings as a contribution to the Lord. It shall belong to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.
The meat of his thanksgiving sacrifice of peace offerings must be eaten on the day he presents it. None of it shall be left until morning.
If the sacrifice he offers is for a vow or is a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day the sacrifice is offered. Whatever remains of it may also be eaten the next day.
Whatever remains of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day must be burned in the fire.

If any of the meat of the sacrifice of the peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who offers it, but will be rejected. Anyone who eats it shall bear the guilt of sin.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it must be burned in the fire. Anyone who is clean may eat the meat.
Anyone who eats meat from the Lord's sacrifice of peace offerings while unclean shall be cut off from their people.
Anyone who touches any human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean creeping creature, and then eats meat from the Lord's sacrifice of peace offerings, shall be cut off from their people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: You must not eat any fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.
The fat of an animal found dead and the fat of one eaten by wild animals may be used for any purpose, but you must not eat it.
For anyone who eats fat from an animal from which an offering is presented to the Lord shall be cut off from their people.
You must not eat any blood, whether of birds or livestock, anywhere you live.
Anyone who eats blood shall be cut off from their people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Whoever presents a peace sacrifice to the Lord shall bring his offering to the Lord from the sacrifice of the burnt offering.
His own hands shall bring the Lord’s offering. He shall bring the fat that is on the chest, and the breast that is set apart as an offering before the Lord.
The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
You shall give the right thigh as an offering set apart for the Lord from your peace offerings.
The right thigh shall belong as a portion to the one among Aaron’s sons who presents the blood and fat of the burnt offering.

For I have taken the breast set apart as an offering and the thigh set apart as an offering from the Israelites, from their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a perpetual due from the Israelites.
This is the anointing portion of Aaron and the anointing portion of his sons from the Lord’s offerings, on the day he is brought forward to serve the Lord.
The Lord commanded the Israelites to give these to them on the day he anointed them, as a perpetual ordinance throughout their generations.
This is the law for the burning of the burnt offering, for the fine flour, for the sin offering, for the offering, for the ordination offering, and for the sacrifice of the burnt offering.
The Lord commanded Moses this on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded him concerning the Israelites, to present their offerings to the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Take Aaron and his sons with him, and take the garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
Gather the whole congregation at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and the whole congregation gathered before the tent of meeting.
Moses said to the whole congregation, “This is what the Lord has commanded to be done.”
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He dressed him in the tunic, tied the sash around him, wrapped him in the robe, and fastened the loincloth around his waist. He put the ephod on him and secured it with the ephod’s belt.
He placed the breastpiece over it and put Knowledge and Truth on the breastpiece.
He placed the turban on his head and put the gold crown, the holy crown, on the front of the turban, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and consecrated them.
He sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and all its utensils; he also anointed the basin and its stand and consecrated them.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, dressed them in tunics, tied sashes around them, and provided them with caps, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull for the sin offering.

He slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood with his finger and sprinkled it on the horns all around the altar, purifying the altar. He poured out the blood at the base of the altar, consecrated it, and made atonement for it.
He took all the fat covering the internal organs, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and Moses burned them on the altar.
The bull, its hide, its flesh, and its dung he burned in the fire outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
Moses slaughtered it and sprinkled some of its blood all around the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces, and Moses burned the heads, the pieces, and the fat.
He washed the internal organs and the legs with water, and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering to the Lord with a pleasing aroma, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
Moses slaughtered it, took some of its blood, and sprinkled it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

He brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses sprinkled some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Moses also sprinkled the blood all around the altar.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat covering the internal organs, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
From the basket of unleavened bread before the Lord, he took one unleavened cake, one cake made with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and on the right thigh.
He placed all these in Aaron’s hands and in his sons’ hands and set them apart as a dedicated offering before the Lord.
Moses took them from their hands and offered them up on the altar, burning them with the burnt offering, so that they would be an ordination offering with a pleasing aroma, an offering to the Lord.
Moses took the breast and set it apart as a dedicated offering before the Lord. It was Moses’ portion from the ram of ordination, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and his sons’ clothes with him. He consecrated Aaron and his clothes, and his sons and his sons’ clothes with him.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Boil the meat at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and eat it there with the bread in the basket of ordination, as I was commanded: ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’
Whatever remains of the meat and the bread you shall burn in the fire.
Do not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed, because your ordination takes seven days.
The Lord commanded that what I have done today be done to make atonement for you.
Stay at the entrance to the tent of meeting day and night for seven days, and fulfill the duties the Lord has given you, so that you do not die, for this is what I was commanded.”
Aaron and his sons did everything the Lord had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of the Israelites.
He said to Aaron, “Take a young bull calf for a sin offering and a ram without blemish for a whole burnt offering, and present them before the Lord.
Tell the Israelites, ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and year-old lambs without blemish for a burnt offering,
and an ox and a ram for a peace offering before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, because today the Lord will appear to you.’”
They took everything Moses had commanded them to take and came before the tent of meeting. The whole congregation approached and stood before the LORD.
Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.”

Moses said to Aaron, “Approach the altar and offer your sin offering and your whole burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then offer the people's offering and make atonement for them, as the LORD commanded.”
Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf for his own sin offering.
Aaron's sons brought him the blood. He dipped his finger in the blood and sprinkled it on the horns of the altar. He poured out the blood at the base of the altar.
He offered the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He burned the meat and the hide in the fire outside the camp.
He slaughtered the whole burnt offering. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he sprinkled it all around the altar.
They handed him the whole burnt offering. He cut it up limb by limb and offered the head on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs and offered the whole burnt offering on the altar.
He presented the people's offering. He took the male goat for the people's sin offering, slaughtered it, and offered it for purification like the first one.
He presented the whole burnt offering and offered it according to its prescribed procedure.
He presented the fine flour, took a handful of it, and offered it on the altar in addition to the morning whole burnt offering.
He slaughtered the bull and the ram as the people's peace offering. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he sprinkled it all around the altar.
And the fat from the bull and the ram, the fat tail, the membrane covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
He placed the fat on the breasts and offered the fat on the altar.
Aaron set apart the breasts and the right thigh as a special offering before the LORD, as Moses had been commanded.
Aaron raised his hands over the people and blessed them. Then he came down after offering the sin offering, the whole burnt offering, and the peace offering.
Moses and Aaron entered the tent of meeting. They came out and blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared before all the people.
Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the fat and the whole burnt offering on the altar. All the people saw it, gave praise, and fell on their faces.

Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his censer. They put fire in them and placed incense in them. They offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, at an improper time, which he had not commanded them to offer.
Fire came out from before the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord.
Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the LORD said: ‘Among those near me I will be shown to be holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.’” And Aaron remained silent.
Moses called Mishael [?] and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle, and said to them, “Come forward and carry your brothers away from the front of the sanctuary to a place outside the camp.”
They approached, picked them up in their tunics, and carried them outside the camp, as Moses had said.

Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons who remained, “Do not uncover your heads or tear your clothes, lest you die and wrath come upon the whole congregation. But let all your brothers, the house of Israel, mourn for those whom the LORD has burned.”
Do not leave the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, or you will die, because the LORD’s anointing oil is upon you. And they did as Moses said.
The LORD said to Aaron:
Do not drink wine or strong drink, you or your sons with you, when you enter the Tent of Meeting, or you will die. This is a lasting statute throughout your generations,
so that you may distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.
You shall teach the Israelites all the statutes that the Lord spoke to them through Moses.
Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his remaining sons, “Take the fine flour left over from the LORD’s offerings, and eat it unleavened beside the altar, because it is most holy.
Eat it in a holy place, because it is your allotted share and the allotted share of your sons with you from the LORD’s offerings, for so I was commanded.

Eat the breast set aside and the thigh set aside in a clean place, you and your sons and daughters with you, because they have been given as your allotted share and the allotted share of your sons with you from the Israelites’ sacrifices of well-being.

They shall bring the thigh set aside and the breast set aside along with the offering of fat, to set them apart before the LORD. They shall belong to you and your sons with you as a lasting statute, as the LORD commanded.”
Moses searched diligently for the goat of the sin offering, but it had been burned. He became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, and said to them:
“Why did you not eat the sin offering in a holy place? For it is most holy, and I gave it to you to bear the congregation’s sin and make atonement for them before the LORD.
Look, none of its blood was brought into the inner sanctuary. You should have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I was commanded, that Aaron and his sons should eat it.”

Aaron said to Moses, “Look, today they offered their sin offerings and their whole burnt offerings before the LORD, and all these things have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been pleasing before the LORD?”
Moses heard this, and it was pleasing in his eyes.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: These are the living creatures you may eat from among all the animals on the earth.
You may eat any animal whose hoof is split and divided in two and that chews the cud.
But these you shall not eat among those that chew the cud or have split hooves: the camel, which chews the cud but does not have split hooves, is unclean for you;
the hyrax, which chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, is unclean for you;
the hare, which chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, is unclean for you;
and the pig, whose hoof is split and divided in two but which does not chew the cud, is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their meat or approach their carcasses. They are unclean for you.
These you may eat from among everything in the water: anything in the water, in the seas or streams, that has fins and scales you may eat.
But anything in the seas or streams that does not have fins and scales, among all the swarming creatures of the water and all the living creatures in the water, is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their meat, and you shall regard their carcasses as unclean.
Anything in the water that does not have fins and scales is unclean for you.
And these you must detest among the birds; they must not be eaten, because they are unclean: the eagle,
and the kite,
and ravens of their various kinds,
and ostriches and hawks of their various kinds,
and the little owl, the fish hawk, and the owl,
and the swan, the pelican, and the bee-eater,
and the stork and herons of their various kinds, and the wild rooster and the peacock.
And all winged insects that walk on all fours are unclean for you.
But these you may eat among all the winged insects that walk on all fours: those that have claws above their feet with which to leap on the ground.
These you may eat among them: locusts of their various kinds and grasshoppers of their various kinds.
And every winged insect that has four feet is unclean for you.
And by these you will become unclean: anyone who touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening.
And anyone who carries their carcasses must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening.
And every animal whose hoof is split but is not divided into two, and that does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Anyone who touches them will be unclean until evening.
Every animal that walks on its paws, among all the animals that walk on four legs, is unclean for you. Anyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And anyone who carries their carcasses must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening, because they are unclean for you.
And these are unclean among all the creatures that crawl on the ground: the weasel, the mouse, and lizards of their various kinds,
and the [?], the mole, the lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are unclean among all the crawling creatures. Anyone who touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.

And anything on which one of them falls when it is dead will become unclean. Any wooden vessel, garment, hide, sack, or any implement used for work must be immersed in water. They will be unclean until evening, and then they will be clean.
And any earthenware vessel into which one of them falls—everything inside it will be unclean, and you must break the vessel.
And any food that is eaten on which water falls will become unclean, and any drink that is drunk from any vessel will become unclean.
And anything on which any part of their carcasses falls will be unclean. An oven or a cooking hearth must be demolished. They are unclean and must be regarded as unclean by you.
But springs, cisterns, and pools of water will remain clean. Anyone who touches their carcasses will be unclean.
And if any part of their carcasses falls on any seed intended for sowing, it remains clean.
If water falls on seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
And if an animal that is clean for you to eat dies, anyone who touches its carcass will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who carries its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
Every crawling creature that crawls on the earth is unclean for you. You shall not eat it.
You shall not eat any creature that crawls on its belly, walks on four legs, or has many legs, among all the crawling creatures that crawl on the earth, because they are unclean.
Do not make yourselves unclean with any crawling creature that crawls on the earth, so that you do not become unclean through them. Do not become unclean through them.
For I am the Lord your God. Sanctify yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean with any crawling creature that crawls on the earth.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. You shall be holy, because I am holy.
This is the law concerning animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the water, and every creature that crawls on the earth,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between animals that may be eaten and animals that may not be eaten.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When a woman conceives and gives birth to a male child, she shall be unclean for seven days. She shall be unclean as she is during the days of her menstruation.
On the eighth day they shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin.
She shall remain in the blood of purification for thirty-three days. She shall not approach anything holy or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
If she gives birth to a female child, she shall be unclean for fourteen days, as during her menstruation. She shall remain in the blood of purification for sixty-six days.

When the days of her purification for a son or a daughter are completed, she shall bring a year-old lamb for a whole burnt offering and a turtledove or a young pigeon for a sin offering to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall offer it before the Lord and make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman who gives birth to a male or female child.

If she cannot afford to bring a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:

“When someone has a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot on the skin of his body, and it becomes a swelling from a leprous lesion on the skin of his body, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who are priests.

They shall bring [?] the priest to the lesion on the skin of his body. If the lesion has spread on the skin of his body, the hair in the lesion has turned white, and the lesion appears deeper than the skin of his body, it is a leprous lesion. The priest shall examine it and declare him unclean.
If the bright spot on the skin of his body is white and does not appear deeper than the skin [?], and the hair has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the affected person for seven days.
The priest shall examine it on the seventh day. If the lesion has remained in place and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall isolate the affected person for another seven days.

The priest shall examine it after another seven days. If the lesion has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall declare the person clean, because it is a rash. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the bright spot spreads on the skin after the priest has examined it and declared the person clean, it shall be shown to the priest again.
The priest shall examine it. If the bright spot has spread on the skin, the priest shall declare the person unclean, because it is leprosy.
When someone has a leprous lesion, he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall examine him. If there is a white swelling on the skin, and it has turned the hair in it white, and there is a sign of raw flesh in the swelling,
It is chronic leprosy in the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and shall not isolate him, because he is unclean.
If leprosy spreads over his skin and covers all his skin, from his head to his feet, wherever the priest can see,
The priest shall examine him. If the leprosy has covered his whole body, he shall declare the lesion clean, for it has all turned white, and he is clean.
But whenever raw flesh appears on him, he shall be unclean.
The priest shall examine the raw flesh and declare the raw flesh unclean. It is unclean because it is leprosy.
But if the raw flesh turns white again, he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall examine it. If the lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the lesion clean, because it is clean.
If a boil develops on a person's skin and heals,
and a white swelling or a white or red bright spot appears where the boil was, it shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall examine it. If it appears lower than the skin and its hair has turned white, the priest shall declare it unclean, because it is a lesion of leprosy that has spread in the boil.
But if the priest sees that there is no white hair in it and that it is not lower than the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate it for seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall declare it unclean, because it is a lesion of leprosy.
But if the bright spot remains in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the boil. The priest shall declare it clean.
If a person has a burn from fire on his skin, and in the scar of the burn there is a bright spot that is white or red or whitish,

the priest shall examine it. If the hair in the bright spot has turned white and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall declare it unclean, because it is a lesion of leprosy.
But if the priest sees that there is no white hair in the bright spot and that it is not lower than the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate it for seven days.
The priest shall examine it on the seventh day. If the bright spot has spread in the skin, the priest shall declare it unclean, because it is a lesion of leprosy.
If the bright spot remains in its place and has not spread in the skin but has faded, it is the scar of the burn. The priest shall declare it clean, because it is the scar of the burn.
If a man or woman has a lesion on the head or beard,

the priest shall examine the lesion. If it appears deeper than the skin and there is thin yellow hair in it, the priest shall declare it unclean, because it is a lesion of leprosy of the head or beard.
But if the priest examines the lesion and it does not appear deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate that lesion for seven days.
The priest shall examine that lesion on the seventh day. If the lesion has not spread, if there is no yellow hair in it, and if the lesion does not appear deeper than the skin,
he shall shave around the lesion but shall not shave the lesion itself. The priest shall isolate the lesion for another seven days.

The priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day. If the lesion has not spread in the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, the priest shall declare it clean. The person shall wash his clothes and become clean.
But if the lesion spreads in the skin after he has been declared clean,
the priest shall examine it. If the lesion has spread in the skin, the priest shall not inquire about yellow hair, because he is unclean.
But if the lesion remains in its place and black hair has grown in it, the lesion is healing, because it is clean. The priest shall declare it clean.
If a man or a woman has a bright, white spot on the skin of their body,
The priest shall examine whether there are white or red spots on the skin of their bodies. It is scurf that has spread on the skin; the person is clean.
If a man's hair falls out and he becomes bald, he is clean.
If his hair falls out at the front of his head, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
If there is a white or red lesion on his bald crown or bald forehead, it is leprosy spreading on his bald crown or bald forehead.
The priest shall examine the swelling of the lesion, whether it has turned white or red on his bald crown or bald forehead, resembling the leprosy found on the skin of his body.
That man has leprosy and is unclean. The priest shall declare him unclean because the lesion is on his head.
Anyone who has leprosy and bears the lesion shall have his clothes torn and his head left unkempt. He shall cover his lips and call himself unclean.
He shall remain unclean as long as he has the lesion. Because he is unclean, he shall live alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
If a garment has a leprous lesion, whether it is a woolen garment or a linen garment,
or in the warp or the weft of linen or wool, or in leather or anything made of leather,
and the lesion is green or red in the garment or leather, or in the warp or weft, or in any leather article, it is a leprous lesion. They shall show it to the priest.
The priest shall examine the affected spot, and the priest shall isolate it for seven days.

The priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day. If the lesion has spread in the garment, or in the warp or weft, or in the leather, or in any leather made into an article for use, it is a lesion of malignant leprosy. It is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, or the warp or the weft of wool or linen, or any leather article in which the affected spot appears. He shall burn it in fire, because it is malignant leprosy.
If the priest sees that the lesion has not spread in the garment, or in the warp or weft, or in any leather article,
the priest shall order them to wash whatever has the lesion, and the priest shall isolate it for another seven days.

The priest shall examine the lesion after it has been washed. If the lesion's appearance has not changed, and the lesion has neither changed nor spread, it is unclean. Burn it in the fire. It is a lesion, whether the article is new or worn.
If the priest sees that the affected spot has faded after it was washed, he shall cut it out of the garment or the leather, or out of the warp or the weft.
If it appears again in the garment, or in the warp or weft, or in any leather article, they shall burn it in the fire, because the lesion has spread in it.
A garment, or warp or weft, or any leather article that has been washed and from which the lesion has disappeared shall be washed a second time and shall be clean.
This is the law concerning a leprous lesion in a woolen or linen garment, or in warp or weft, or in any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
This shall be the law concerning a person with leprosy on the day he is cleansed: he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall examine whether the man's leprous lesion has healed.
The priest shall order them to bring two live, clean birds, cedarwood, scarlet dye, and hyssop for the person being cleansed.
The priest shall order them to slaughter one bird in an earthenware vessel over spring water.

He shall take the other bird, the living one, together with the cedarwood, scarlet dye, and hyssop, and dip them, along with the living bird, in the blood of the bird slaughtered over the spring water.
He shall sprinkle the person being cleansed of leprosy seven times, and that person shall be clean. He shall release the living bird to fly into the open field.

The person being cleansed shall wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water, and he shall be clean. Afterward he may enter the camp, but he shall stay outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair—his head, his beard, and his eyebrows. He shall shave off all his hair, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in water, and he shall be clean.
On the eighth day he must take two male lambs without blemish, one year-old ewe lamb without blemish, three tenth-measures of sifted fine flour mixed with oil, and a log-measure of oil.
The priest who cleanses him must present the man being cleansed, together with these things, before the Lord at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest must take one lamb and offer it as a sin offering, together with the log-measure of oil. The priest must set them apart as a dedicated offering before the Lord.
He must slaughter the lamb in the place where he slaughters the sin offering and the whole burnt offering, in a holy place. For the offering for sin belongs to the priest; it is most holy.
The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering and sprinkle it on the right earlobe of the man being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take one measure of oil and pour it into the priest’s left hand.
The priest must dip his right finger into the oil in his left hand, and with his finger the priest must sprinkle some of the oil seven times before the Lord.

From the oil remaining in his hand, the priest must sprinkle some on the right earlobe of the man being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, where the blood of the sin offering was placed.
The priest must put the oil left in his hand on the head of the man being cleansed. The priest must make atonement for him before the Lord.
The priest must offer the sin offering and make atonement for the man being cleansed from his uncleanness. Afterward he must slaughter the whole burnt offering.
The priest must offer up the whole burnt offering and the fine flour on the altar. The priest must make atonement for him, and he will be clean.

If he is poor and cannot afford these things, he must take one lamb as a sin offering, to be set apart as a dedicated offering so that atonement may be made for him, one tenth of a seah of sifted flour mixed with oil as an offering, and one log-measure of oil.
He must also take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford. One must be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he must bring them to the priest to cleanse him, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, before the Lord.
The priest must take one lamb and the log-measure of oil, and the priest must set them apart as a dedicated offering before the Lord.

He must slaughter the lamb for the sin offering. The priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering and sprinkle it on the right earlobe of the man being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest must pour some of the oil into his own left hand.
With his right finger, the priest must sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the Lord.

The priest must sprinkle some of the oil in his hand on the right earlobe of the man being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, where the blood of the sin offering was placed.
He must sprinkle the oil remaining in the priest’s hand on the head of the man being cleansed and make atonement for him before the Lord.
He must offer some of the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford.
One must be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering, together with the fine flour. The priest must make atonement before the Lord for the man being cleansed.
This is the law for someone who has an affliction of leprosy and cannot afford what is required for his cleansing.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
“When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as an inheritance, and I put an affliction of leprosy in a house in the land you possess,
the owner of the house must come and inform the priest, saying to him, ‘Something like an affliction of leprosy has appeared to me in the house.’
The priest shall order the house to be emptied before he goes in to inspect the affected area, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. Afterward the priest shall enter.
He shall inspect the affected area. If the affected area on the wall of the house has greenish or reddish patches that appear deeper than the wall,
the priest shall leave the house, stand at its doorway, and shut up that house for seven days.
The priest shall return on the seventh day and see whether the affected area has spread on the wall of the house.
The priest shall give orders, and they shall remove the stones that have the leprous infection in them and throw them outside the town in an unclean place.
They shall scrape the inside of that house all around and throw the plaster they have scraped off outside the town in an unclean place.
They shall take other stones and put them in place of the stones, and they shall take fresh plaster and plaster the house.
If the affected area spreads and increases in the house after the stones have been removed and after the house has been scraped and plastered,
the priest shall enter and see whether the affected area has spread in the house. It is a severe leprous disease in the house; it is unclean.
They shall tear down the house—its stones, its timbers, and all its plaster—and carry it outside the town to an unclean place and burn it with fire.
Anyone who enters the house during any of the days when it is shut up shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sleeps in the house shall wash his clothes, and anyone who eats in the house shall wash his clothes.
If the priest enters and sees that the affected area has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare that house clean, because the affected area has healed.
For the cleansing of the house he shall take two living, clean birds, cedarwood, hyssop, and scarlet dye. The priest shall give the order,
and they shall slaughter one bird in an earthenware vessel over spring water.
He shall take the other, living bird, the cedarwood, the hyssop, and the scarlet dye, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in fresh water. He shall sprinkle that house seven times.
He shall cleanse the house with the bird's blood, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedarwood, the hyssop, and the scarlet dye.
He shall release the living bird outside the town into the open country. He shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
This shall be the law for every leprous affliction and for an affected area,
for leprous disease in clothing or in a house,
and for a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot,
and for distinguishing between the unclean and the clean. This is the law concerning leprous disease.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.
This shall be the uncleanness of his discharge: whether his body flows with the discharge or his body is blocked by the discharge, it is his uncleanness.
Every bed on which the man with the discharge lies shall be unclean, and every object on which he sits shall be unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits on an object on which the man with a discharge has sat must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
If the man with a discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anything on which the man with a discharge rides will be unclean.
Anyone who touches anything that is under him will be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries these things must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches the man with a discharge when he has not washed his hands in water must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
An earthenware vessel that the man with a discharge touches must be broken, and every wooden or bronze vessel must be rinsed in water.

When the man with a discharge becomes free of his discharge, he must count off seven days for himself and be cleansed. He must wash his clothes and bathe his body in running water, and he will be clean.
On the eighth day he must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them before the Lord to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.
The priest must offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a whole burnt offering. The priest must make atonement for him before the Lord because of his discharge.
If a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Any cloth or bedding on which semen falls must be washed in water, and it will be unclean until evening.
If a man has sexual intercourse with a woman, with an emission of semen, they must bathe in water, and they will be unclean until evening.
When a woman has a discharge of blood, with the discharge coming from her body, she must remain in her menstrual impurity for seven days. Anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
Anything on which she lies during her menstrual impurity will be unclean, and anything on which she sits will be unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches any object on which she sits must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
If someone touches the bedding or the object on which she sits, he will be unclean until evening.
If a man sleeps with her and any of her menstrual discharge gets on him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bedding on which he lies will be unclean.

When a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual period, or if her discharge continues beyond her menstrual period, all the days when she has the discharge in her uncleanness will be like the days of her menstrual period, and she will be unclean.

Any bedding on which she lies throughout the days of her discharge will be like her bedding during her menstrual period. Any object on which she sits will be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her menstrual period.
Anyone who touches them will become unclean. He must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
When she becomes free of her discharge, she must count off seven days for herself, and afterward she will be clean.
On the eighth day she must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest must offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest must make atonement for her before the Lord because of her unclean discharge.
You shall warn the Israelites against their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness and do not defile my tabernacle that is among them.
This shall be the law for anyone who has a discharge, and for anyone who emits semen during intercourse and becomes unclean through it,
and for a menstruating woman during her period, and for anyone with a discharge, whether male or female, during their discharge, and for a man who sleeps with an unclean woman.
The Lord spoke with Moses after the death of Aaron’s two sons, when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord and died.

The Lord said to Moses, “Speak with your brother Aaron, so that he does not enter the sanctuary at just any time, behind the curtain, before the mercy seat on the ark, lest he die. For I appear in the cloud above the mercy seat.
Aaron shall enter the sanctuary with these: a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a whole burnt offering.

He shall put on a sacred linen tunic, and linen undergarments shall cover his body. He shall tie a linen sash around himself and put a linen turban on his head, for these are sacred garments. He shall bathe his body in water and put them on.
From the congregation of the Israelites he shall take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron shall offer his own bull as a sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
He shall take the two male goats and present them alive before the Lord at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Aaron shall cast lots over the two male goats: one lot for the Lord and one lot for Azazel.
Aaron shall bring forward the male goat on which the Lord’s lot fell and offer it as a sin offering.
The male goat on which Azazel’s lot fell shall stand alive before the Lord, so that atonement may be made over it, and they shall send it away to Azazel in the wilderness.
Aaron shall offer his own bull as a sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. He shall slaughter the bull for the sin offering.
He shall take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the Lord, and two handfuls of incense made from fragrant spices, and go behind the curtain.
He shall put the incense on the fire before the Lord, and the cloud of incense shall cover the mercy seat that is over the testimony, so that he does not die.

He shall take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the eastern face of the atonement cover. In front of the atonement cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger.

He shall slaughter the male goat as the people’s sin offering and bring its blood behind the curtain. He shall do with its blood as he did with the bull’s blood, sprinkling it on the mercy seat and in front of the mercy seat.

He shall make atonement for the sanctuary because of the Israelites’ uncleanness, their wrongdoing, and all their sins. He shall do the same for the Tent of Meeting, which stands among them in the midst of their uncleanness.

No one shall be in the Tent of Meeting from the time he enters to make atonement in the sanctuary until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself and his household, and he shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites.
He shall go out to the altar before the Lord and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull’s blood and some of the male goat’s blood and sprinkle it on the horns of the altar all around.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleansing it and making it holy from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
When he has finished making atonement for the holy places, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he shall bring forward the living male goat.

Aaron shall place both his hands on the head of the living male goat and confess over it all the Israelites’ guilt, all their wrongdoing, and all their sins. He shall place them on the male goat’s head and send it away into the wilderness through a man who is ready for the task.
The male goat shall carry all their wrongdoing upon itself to a desolate land, and the man shall release the male goat in the wilderness.
Aaron shall enter the Tent of Meeting and take off the linen garments he wore when he entered the sanctuary, and he shall leave them there.
He must bathe his body in water in a holy place, put on his clothes, and come out. He must offer his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
He shall offer the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
The person who sends the goat away to Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe in water. Afterward he may enter the camp.

The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the sanctuary to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp. Their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned in the fire.
The person who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Then he may enter the camp.
This must be a lasting law for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you must humble yourselves and do no work, neither you nor those who turn to me and live among you.
For on this day atonement shall be made for you, so that you may be cleansed from all your sins. Before the Lord you shall be clean.
It is a Sabbath of rest for you, and you must humble yourselves. This is a lasting law.
The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve in his father's place must make atonement. He must put on the linen garments, the holy clothes.
He must make atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting, and the altar. He must also make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
This must be a lasting law for you: atonement must be made for the Israelites for all their sins once a year. And they did as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak with Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, and tell them: This is what the Lord has commanded:
Any Israelite who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat inside the camp, or slaughters it outside the camp,

and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the Lord before the Lord's tabernacle, will be held guilty of bloodshed, because he has shed blood. That man must be cut off from his people.

This is so that the Israelites will bring the sacrifices they slaughter in the open fields to the Lord, to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and sacrifice them as peace offerings to the Lord.
The priest must sprinkle the blood on the Lord's altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the demons they stray after. This must be a lasting law for them throughout their generations.
Tell them: Anyone from the house of Israel, or from those who turn to me and live among you, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it before the Lord—that man must be cut off from his people.
If anyone from Israel, or from those who turn to me and live in Israel, eats blood, I will direct my anger against the person who eats blood and cut that person off from their people.
For the life of the flesh is the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives, because it is the blood that makes atonement for life.
That is why I said to the Israelites: None of you may eat blood, and those who turn to me and live with you must not eat blood.
Anyone from the Israelites, or from those who turn to me and live among you, who hunts and catches an animal or bird that may be eaten must pour out its blood and cover it with dust.
For the life of all flesh is the blood. Tell the Israelites: You must not eat the blood of any flesh, because the life of all flesh is the blood. Anyone who eats it must be cut off.

Anyone who eats an animal that has died or has been torn by a wild animal, whether one of you or one of those who turn to me and live among you, must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash his clothes or bathe his body, he must bear the guilt of his sin.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: I am the Lord your God.
You must not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you lived. You must not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you, and you must not live by their laws.
Instead, carry out my judgments, keep my commandments, and live by them. I am the Lord your God.
Keep my commandments and my judgments. The person who carries them out will live by them. I am the Lord.
None of you must approach any close blood relative to uncover their nakedness. I am the Lord.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you must not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife, for it is your father’s nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether born to your father or to another man.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for their nakedness is your own nakedness.
The daughter of your father's wife, born to your father, is your sister. You must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister, for she is your father's close relative.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, because she is your mother's close relative.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your uncle's wife. You must not approach his wife, because she is your uncle's wife. You must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover your daughter-in-law's nakedness. Because she is your son's wife, you must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife, for it is your brother's nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter, or approach her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover their nakedness. They are close relatives, and it is wickedness.
You must not marry a woman in addition to her sister, causing her distress and uncovering the other woman's nakedness alongside her during her lifetime.
You must not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness during her menstrual uncleanness.
You must not deposit your semen in your neighbor's wife through intercourse and defile yourself with her.
You must not deposit any of your semen to make a foreign woman pregnant, and you must not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord.
You must not lie with a male as one lies with a woman, because it is unclean.
You must not deposit your semen in any animal and defile yourself with it. A woman must not stand before an animal to be mounted by it, because it is uncleanness.
Do not defile yourselves by any of these things, because the nations that I am driving out before you have defiled themselves by all these things.
The land became defiled, and I punished it for its wrongdoing, and the land cast out its inhabitants.
Keep my statutes and my judgments, and do not commit any of these sins—neither you nor those who turn to me and live among you.
For the people of the land who were there before you committed all these sins, and the land became defiled.
Do not defile the land, so that it does not cast you out as it cast out the nation that was there before you.
For whoever commits any one of all these sins—those who do them shall perish from among their people.
Keep my requirements, and do not follow the sinful customs practiced by those before you, or defile yourselves with them. I am the Lord your God.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak to the whole congregation of the Israelites and tell them: Be holy, because I am holy. I am the Lord your God.
Each of you must fear his father and his mother. Keep my commandments, because I am the Lord your God.
Do not turn to demons, and do not make cast-metal gods for yourselves. I am the Lord your God.
When you offer sacrifices of well-being to the Lord, offer them so that they will be accepted.
They shall be eaten on the day they are sacrificed, and they may be eaten the next day. Whatever remains until the third day shall be burned in the fire and shall not be eaten.
If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is detestable and will not be accepted.
Whoever eats any of it shall bear the sin, because he has profaned what is holy to the Lord. That person shall perish from among her people.
When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap the edges of your fields completely, and you shall not gather the gleanings of your harvest.
Do not glean your vineyards, and do not gather the fallen fruit of your olive trees. Instead, leave them for the poor and for those who turn to me, because I am the Lord your God.
Do not steal. Do not lie. Do not deceive one another.
Do not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the Lord.
Do not oppress your neighbor or treat him with violence. Do not keep a hired worker’s wages with you overnight until morning.
Do not revile the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind. Instead, fear your God. I am the Lord.
Do not act unjustly in judgment. Do not show partiality to the poor or to the powerful. Instead, judge your neighbor justly.
You shall not slander your people, and you shall not act against your neighbor’s life, for I am the Lord.
Do not hate your brother in your heart. Instead, firmly rebuke your neighbor, so that you do not bear sin because of him.
Do not harbor hostility toward the members of your people. Instead, love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord.
Keep my commandments. Do not crossbreed your livestock. Do not sow your fields with mixed seed. Do not wear garments woven from mixed materials.

If a man has sexual intercourse with a woman who is a slave bought for a man, and she has not been redeemed or given her freedom, they shall be subjected to questioning, but they shall not be put to death, because she had not been freed.
He shall bring his offering to the Lord, to the entrance of the tent of meeting: a ram as a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord with the ram of the sin offering, for the sin he committed, and the sin he committed shall be forgiven him.
When you enter the land and plant any trees for food, leave them alone for three years and do not eat any of their fruit.
In the fourth year, all their fruit shall be holy, an offering of praise to the Lord.
In the fifth year, eat their fruit, and their yield will increase for you. I am the Lord your God.
Do not eat blood. Do not look for omens in birds. Do not practice divination.
Do not let the hair of your heads grow long, and do not disfigure the edges of your beards.
Do not make cuts in your flesh for the dead, and do not make tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the Lord.
Do not allow your daughter to prostitute herself, so that the land does not become a prostitute and become filled with sin.
Instead, keep my commandments and revere my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
Do not follow mediums and spiritists, and do not consult them, so that you do not become unclean through them. I am the Lord your God.
Stand up in the presence of an old man, honor anyone older than you, and fear your God. I am the Lord.
When someone who turns to me lives among you, do not mistreat him.
Instead, he is to be like you and one of you. Love those who turn to me and live among you as yourselves, because you too were foreigners living in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
Do not act unjustly in judgment, in the scales, in weights, or in measures.
You must have honest scales, honest weights, honest measures, and an honest liquid measure. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep all my commandments and all my laws, and carry them out. I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:

Tell the Israelites: Any man among the Israelites or among those who turn to me and live in Israel who deposits his seed in a foreign woman must be put to death. The people of the land must stone him with stones.
I will direct my anger against that man and destroy him from among his people, because he deposited his seed in a foreign woman, defiling my sanctuary and defiling my holy name.
If the people of the land avert their eyes from that man who deposited his seed in a foreign woman and do not put him to death,
I will act in anger against that man and his family. I will destroy him and all who go astray after him from among their people, because they go astray after foreign women.
If a person follows mediums and spiritists and goes astray after them, I will direct my anger against that person and destroy that person from among their people.
Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am the Lord your God.
Keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the Lord who makes you holy.
A man who curses his father or his mother must be put to death. He has cursed his father or his mother; his blood is on his own head.
