A man who commits adultery with another man's wife, who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife—both the adulterer and the adulteress must be put to death.
A man who sleeps with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them must be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.
If a man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall certainly be put to death, because they have committed a sin. Their blood is on their own heads.
If a man sleeps with a male as one sleeps with a woman, they have committed a filthy act. Both of them must be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.
If a man marries a woman and her mother, it is a sin. They must burn him and the women with fire, so that there is no sin among you.
If a man sleeps with an animal, he shall certainly be put to death, and the animal shall also be stoned.
If a woman approaches an animal to be mounted by it, kill the woman and the animal as well. They must certainly be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.

If a man marries his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she also sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace. They must be destroyed in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; they must bear their guilt.
If a man sleeps with a menstruating woman and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her flow, and she has exposed the source of her blood. Both of them must be destroyed from among their people.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or your father's sister, because they are close relatives. Nakedness [?]. They must bear their guilt.
If a man sleeps with his uncle's wife, he has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They must bear their sin and die childless.
If a man marries his brother's wife, it is wrongdoing, because he has uncovered his brother's nakedness. They will be childless.
Keep all my commandments and my judgments, and carry them out, so that the land into which I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out.
You must not follow the laws of the nations that I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I was disgusted with them.
I told you, 'You will inherit their land, and I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey.' I am the Lord your God, who separated you from the nations.

Distinguish between clean and unclean animals, and between clean and unclean birds. Do not make yourselves unclean through animals, birds, or any creature that crawls on the ground that I have set apart for you as unclean.
You must be holy, because I, the Lord, am holy. I have separated you from the nations to be mine.
A man or woman who has a spirit of the dead or spirits of divination must certainly be put to death. They must be stoned with stones; their blood is on their own heads.
The Lord said to Moses, 'Tell the priests, the sons of Aaron, that they must not make themselves unclean for a dead person among their people,'
except for a close relative: his father, his mother, his son, his daughter, or his brother,
or his virgin sister who is close to him and has not married a man. For her he may make himself unclean.
He must not make himself unclean for a leader of his people and so defile himself.
They must not shave bald patches on their heads, shave the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their bodies.
Instead, they must be holy to their God and must not profane the name of their God, because they present the Lord's offerings, the food of their God. They must be holy.
They must not marry a woman who is a prostitute or is defiled, and they must not marry a woman divorced by her husband, because the priest is holy to his God.
Treat him as holy, because he presents the food of your God. He must be holy to you, because he is holy. I am the Lord who makes you holy.
When a priest’s daughter begins to prostitute herself, she defiles her father. She shall be burned with fire.
The priest who is highest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil is poured and who is ordained to wear the vestments, must not uncover his head or tear his garments.
He must not go in where there is any dead person, nor defile himself for his father or his mother.
He must not leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, because the crown of his God's anointing oil is upon him. I am the Lord.
He must marry a virgin.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman defiled by prostitution—none of these. Instead, he must marry a virgin from his own people.
He must not defile his offspring among his people, because I am the Lord who makes him holy.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak with Aaron and tell him: Throughout their generations, no man among your descendants who has a physical defect may approach to offer the bread of his God.
For no man who has a physical defect may approach: a man who is lame or blind, has a disfigured nose, or has a torn ear;
or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand;
or is hunched over or undersized, has lost his eyebrows, has impaired sight or a white film over his eyes, has a scabby disease or a skin eruption, or has only one testicle.
No man among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall approach to present the Lord’s offering. Because he has a defect, he shall not approach to present the food of his God.
He may eat the bread of his God, [?] the most holy things, from the holy things.
But he must not enter inside the doorway or approach the altar, because he has a physical defect. He must not profane my sanctuary, for I am the Lord who makes them holy.
Moses told this to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the Israelites.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Tell Aaron and his sons to keep away from the holy offerings of the Israelites and not defile my holy name, because they consecrate these offerings to me. I am the Lord.

Tell them: Throughout their generations, any man among all your descendants who approaches the holy offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the Lord while he is unclean—that person shall perish from before my eyes. I am the Lord.

Any man among Aaron’s descendants who has a leprous disease or a discharge must not eat any of the holy offerings until he becomes clean. Anyone who touches anything made unclean by a corpse, or a man who has an emission of semen,
or a man who touches any crawling creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean through any kind of uncleanness—
the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening. He must not eat any of the holy offerings unless he has washed his body with water.
At sunset he shall become clean, and then he may eat the holy offerings, because they are his food.
He must not eat the carcass of an animal torn by a wild beast, so that he does not become unclean through it. I am the Lord.
They must observe my requirements, so that they do not bring sins upon themselves and die because of them, because they have defiled themselves. I am the Lord who makes them holy.
No outsider may eat a holy offering. A priest’s resident guest or hired worker must not eat a holy offering.
But when a priest buys a person with his own money, that person may eat his food. Those born in his household may also eat his food.
If a priest’s daughter marries an outsider, she must not eat any of the holy contributions.
But if a priest’s daughter is widowed or divorced, has no children, and returns to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat her father’s food. No outsider, however, may eat it.
If a man eats a holy offering by mistake, he must add one-fifth to it and give the holy offering to the priest.
The Israelites shall not profane the holy offerings that they set apart for the Lord.
They will bring guilt and sins upon themselves when they eat their holy offerings, for I am the Lord who makes them holy.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:

Speak with Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, and tell them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of those who have turned to me and live in Israel, who presents his offering, whether from any of their vows or any of their voluntary contributions that they offer to the Lord as a whole burnt offering—
For acceptance, a male without a defect, from the cattle, lambs, or goats.
Do not offer anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.
When someone offers a peace offering to the Lord, to fulfill a vow or as a voluntary offering, from the cattle or goats, it must be without a defect. It will be accepted if it has no defect at all.
Do not offer to the Lord any animal that is blind, broken, maimed, has a growth, has mange, or has scabs. Do not place an offering from any of these on the altar for the Lord.
You may offer an ox or a lamb whose ear is torn or whose tail is short as a voluntary offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow.
Do not offer to the Lord an animal that has been crushed, slit, or mutilated, and do not do this in your land.
Do not offer any of these as the food of your God from the hand of a foreigner. Because they are damaged and have defects, they will not be accepted from you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
When a calf, a lamb, or a young goat is born, it must remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day onward, it may be accepted as an offering to the Lord.
Do not slaughter a cow or a sheep together with its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to the Lord, sacrifice it so that it may be accepted.
It must be eaten that same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the Lord.
Keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the Lord.
You shall not profane my holy name, so that I may be sanctified among the Israelites. I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
Who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: The Lord’s festivals, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies—these are my festivals.
You shall work for six days, but the seventh day shall be a Sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord. You must not do any work. It is a Sabbath to the Lord wherever you live.
These are the Lord’s festivals, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies at their appointed times.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, is the Lord’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this same month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread to the Lord. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.
On the first day you shall have a sacred assembly. You must not do any ordinary work.
Present an offering to the Lord for seven days. On the seventh day there shall be a sacred assembly, and you shall not do any ordinary work.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, bring a sheaf of the first of your harvest to the priest.
He shall present the sheaf before the Lord so that it may be accepted. After another day, the priest shall present it.
On the day when you present the sheaf, you shall offer a year-old lamb without a defect as a whole burnt offering to the Lord.
Its grain offering shall be two tenths of two seahs of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering to the Lord for a pleasing aroma. Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.

You shall not eat bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until this day, until the day when you bring the offering to your God. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Count for yourselves from the day after that day, from the day when you bring the sheaf set apart as an offering. There shall be seven complete [?] weeks.
Count fifty days, until after the seventh week, and offer the Lord a grain offering from the new harvest.
From your homes bring bread as a presentation offering: two [?] made from two tenths of fine flour. They shall be baked with yeast, as firstfruits to the Lord.

Along with the bread, offer seven year-old lambs without blemish, one young bull, and two rams. They shall be a whole burnt offering to the Lord, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, an offering for a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of well-being.

The priest shall present them with the bread of the firstfruits as a presentation offering before the Lord, together with the two lambs. They shall be holy before the Lord and shall belong to the priest.
Proclaim this day a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations, wherever you live.

When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap the edges of your fields completely, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest. Instead, leave them for the poor and for those who turn to me. I am the Lord your God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: On the first day of the seventh month, you shall have a day of rest and a memorial proclaimed with a trumpet blast. You shall have a sacred assembly.
You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall bring an offering to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him: Speak to the Israelites and tell them:
On the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. You shall hold a holy assembly, humble yourselves, and bring an offering to the Lord.
You shall do no work on that day, because it is the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for you before the Lord your God.
For anyone who does not humble themselves on that day shall perish from among their people.
Anyone who does any work on that day—I will destroy that person from among their people.
You shall do no work. This is a lasting ordinance throughout your generations, wherever you live.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall humble yourselves. On the ninth day of the month, in the evening, at twilight, from evening until evening, you shall observe your Sabbath rest.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month, celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days before the Lord.
On the first day you shall hold a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
For seven days bring an offering to the Lord. On the eighth day you shall hold a holy assembly and bring an offering to the Lord. You shall gather together, and you shall do no ordinary work.

These are the Lord’s festivals, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, and during them you shall bring offerings to the Lord: whole burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and sacrifices, each on its appointed day.
These are in addition to the Lord’s Sabbaths, your offerings, your gifts, all your vows, and all the contributions that you give to the Lord.

However, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you gather in the produce of the land, celebrate the Lord’s festival for seven days. On the first day there shall be a cessation of work, and on the eighth day there shall be rest.
On the first day, take for yourselves fruit from beautiful trees: citrons, palm fronds, myrtle, and willows. Rejoice before the Lord your God for seven days, all of you of the house of Israel.
Celebrate this festival to the Lord for seven days each year. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations. Celebrate it in the seventh month.
Live in shelters for seven days. All those of the house of Israel shall live in shelters.
So that your generations may know that I made the Israelites live in shelters when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
Moses told the Israelites about the festivals of the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Command the Israelites to bring you pure pressed olive oil to keep the lamps burning continually.
Outside the entrance of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall tend them from evening until morning before the Lord continually. This is a lasting statute throughout your generations.
He shall arrange the lamps on the great lampstand before the Lord continually.
Take fine flour and bake twelve cakes [?], each cake [?] made from two-tenths.
Arrange them in two rows, six in each row, on the pure table before the Lord.
Put pure frankincense on the rows before the Lord. It shall serve as a memorial for the bread and as an offering to the Lord.
On the sixth day Aaron shall arrange them before the Lord continually, on behalf of the Israelites, as an everlasting covenant.
It shall belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy for him among the offerings of the Lord. This is a lasting statute.
The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the Israelites. The Israelite woman's son and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
The Israelite woman's son pronounced the Name and cursed. They brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They held him in custody so that the Lord’s own word would make the matter clear to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Bring the man who cursed outside the camp. Let everyone who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let the whole congregation stone him.
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Whenever anyone curses his God, he shall bear his sin.

Whoever pronounces the name of the Lord shall certainly be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him. Whether someone who turns to me or an Israelite, whoever pronounces my name shall be put to death.
If anyone kills a human being, he shall certainly be put to death.
Whoever kills an animal shall make restitution, life for life.
If anyone injures his neighbor, just as he injured his neighbor, so shall it be done to him.
Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has injured his neighbor, so it shall be done to him.
Whoever kills an animal shall pay for it, and whoever kills a person shall be put to death.
You shall have one law. It shall be the same for someone who turns to me and for an Israelite. I am the Lord your God.
Moses spoke to the Israelites. They brought the man who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died. The Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land that I am giving you as an inheritance, the land shall observe a Sabbath for the Lord.
For six years you shall sow your fields, and for six years you shall prune your vineyards, and for six years you shall gather your crops.
But in the seventh year the land shall have a Sabbath of complete rest. It shall be a Sabbath for the Lord for you. You shall not sow your fields or prune your vineyards.
Do not reap what grows on its own from your harvest, and do not gather the grapes from your untended vines. It shall be a year of rest for the land.
What the land produces during its rest shall be food for you, your male and female slaves, your hired workers, and the resident foreigners who live with you.
All its produce shall also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
Count off seven sabbatical cycles of years for yourselves, seven years seven times. The duration of these seven weeks of years shall be forty-nine years.
Sound the trumpet of jubilation on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement, sound the trumpet throughout your land.

Set apart the fiftieth year as holy, and proclaim freedom throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a Jubilee for you. Each of you shall return to his ancestral property, and each to his family.
The fiftieth year shall be a Jubilee for you. Do not sow your land, reap what grows on its own, or gather grapes from its untended vines.
For it is a Jubilee and shall be holy to you. Eat the produce directly from the fields.
In this year of Jubilee, each of you shall return to his ancestral property.
If you sell something to your neighbor or buy something from your neighbor, do not wrong one another.
Buy from your neighbor according to the number of years since the Jubilee, and he shall sell to you according to the number of years of harvest.

The greater the number of years, the higher you shall make its purchase price; the fewer the years, the lower you shall make its purchase price. For it is a number of years of harvest that he is selling you.
Do not wrong one another, but fear your God, for I am the Lord your God.
Carry out my commandments, and keep my laws and obey them. Then you shall live securely in the land.
The land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat your fill and live securely in it.
If you say, “What shall we eat in the seventh year, since we will neither sow nor gather its crops?”
I will send you my blessings in the sixth year, and it shall produce a harvest sufficient for three years.
You shall sow in the eighth year and eat from the old harvest until the ninth year. Until the harvest comes in, you shall continue eating the old produce.
The land must never be sold permanently, for the land is mine, and you are foreigners and temporary residents with me.
Throughout all the land you hold as your inheritance, you must allow the land to be redeemed.
If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his inherited property, his nearest relative shall come and redeem what his brother sold.
If there is no one to redeem it, but he gains the means and finds enough to redeem it,
he shall calculate the years since its sale and return the remaining value to the man who bought it from him. Then he shall return to his ancestral property.

But if he does not gain the means to repay him, the sale shall remain valid for the buyer until the year of Jubilee. At the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his ancestral property.
If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled town, he shall have the right to redeem it until a year from its sale has passed. His right of redemption shall last from one anniversary to the next.

If it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled town shall belong permanently to the buyer and his descendants. It shall not be released from his possession at the Jubilee.
But houses in unwalled settlements shall be treated as fields in the countryside. They shall be subject to redemption, and the property shall be released at the Jubilee.
As for the towns of the Levites and the houses in the towns belonging to them, the Levites shall always have the right to redeem them.

If anyone redeems property from the Levites, the house and the town of his inheritance shall be released from the sale at the Jubilee, because the houses in the Levites’ towns are their inheritance among the Israelites.
The fields on the outskirts of their towns must not be sold, because they are their permanent possession.
If your brother becomes poor and his means fail while he is with you, do not take hold of him as a resident alien or a temporary resident. Let him live with you.
Do not take interest or profit from him. Fear your God, and let your brother live with you.
Do not lend him your money at interest or give him your food for profit.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor and is sold to you, do not make him do the work of a slave.
He shall be with you as a hired worker or a temporary resident. He shall remain with you until the year of Jubilee.
Then he shall leave you, together with his children, and return to his family. He shall return to his father’s inheritance.
For they are my slaves, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves are sold.
Do not make him work harshly, but fear your God.
The male and female slaves you own shall come from the nations around you. From them you may buy male and female slaves.

You may also acquire slaves from the children of the temporary residents living among you and from their families who are with you, whom they have fathered in your land. They shall become your property.

You may pass them on to your children after you as inherited property. You may make them work as slaves permanently. But you must not make your brothers, the Israelites, work harshly, one brother treating another this way.

If a resident alien or temporary resident among you becomes prosperous, and your brother becomes poor beside him and is sold to the resident alien or temporary resident among you, or to someone born into the resident alien’s family among you,
he shall have the right to be redeemed after he has been sold. One of his brothers may redeem him.
His uncle or his uncle’s son may redeem him, or a close blood relative from his family may redeem him. Or, if he gains sufficient means, he may redeem himself.

He shall calculate with his buyer the time from the year he was sold to him until the year of Jubilee. His sale price shall be reckoned according to the number of years. His time with him shall be counted like the days of a hired worker.
If many years still remain, he shall pay back his redemption price in proportion to them, based on the money paid for him.
If only a few years remain until the year of Jubilee, he shall calculate with him and pay back his redemption price in proportion to his remaining years.
He shall be with him as a worker hired year by year. His owner must not make him work harshly before your eyes.
If he is not redeemed by these means, he shall go free in the year of Jubilee, together with his children.
For the Israelites belong to me as slaves. They are my slaves, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
Do not make idols or images for yourselves, and do not set up sacred pillars for yourselves. Do not make stones for worship in your land, and do not bow down to them. I am the Lord your God.
Keep my commandments and revere my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
If you follow my laws, keep my commandments, and carry them out,
I will give you rain at its proper times. The land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.
Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until sowing time. You will eat your bread and be satisfied, and you will live securely in your land.
I will give peace in your land. You will lie down with no one to frighten you. I will remove dangerous wild animals from the land, and no sword will pass through your land.
You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will turn toward you, make you increase, and multiply you. I will establish my covenant with you.
You will eat food from stores long kept, and you will clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will place my dwelling among you, and I will not detest you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the yoke of your slavery and made you walk upright.
But if you do not listen to me and do not carry out all these commandments,
if you reject my laws, detest my judgments, do not carry out all my commandments, and break my covenants,

then I too will do this to you: I will bring terror upon you, leprosy, a scaly disease, and dysentery that destroy the eyes and drain away life. You will sow your seed in vain, and your enemies will eat it.
I will turn my anger against you, and you will be defeated before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee even when no one is pursuing you.
If even after these things you do not listen to me, I will punish you sevenfold for your sins.
I will break your proud strength. I will make your skies like iron and your land like bronze.
Your strength will be exhausted in vain. Your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not bear their fruit.
If you act with hostility toward me and refuse to listen to me, I will bring sevenfold more plagues upon you for your sins.
I will send wild animals against you. They will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers, and your roads will become deserted.
If even after these things you will not accept correction, but act with hostility toward me,
then I too will act with hostility toward you, and I myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
I will bring a sword against you to exact vengeance for the covenant. You will flee to your towns, and I will send a plague among you. You will be handed over to your enemies.
I will cut off your supply of grain. Ten women will bake your bread in one oven, and they will give you your bread by weight. You will eat but will not be satisfied.
If even after these things you do not listen to me, but act with hostility toward me,
I too will deal with you in anger and hostility, and I will punish you sevenfold for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your high places and demolish your idols. I will throw your corpses onto the corpses of your idols, and I will detest you.
I will turn your towns into ruins and lay your sanctuary waste. I will not smell your pleasing fragrance.
I myself will lay the land waste, and your enemies who live in it will be appalled at it.
I will scatter you among the nations and draw a sword after you. Your land shall become a wasteland, and your towns shall become ruins.
Then the land will enjoy its sabbaths throughout all the days of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.
Throughout all the days of its desolation it will rest, because it did not rest during your sabbaths when you lived in it.

As for those of you who remain, I will put fear into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a rustling leaf will chase them, and they will flee as people flee from a sword. They will fall though no one is pursuing them.
They will stumble over one another as though fleeing from a sword, though no one is pursuing them. They will have no strength to stand before their enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
Those of you who remain will waste away because of their guilt in the land of their enemies. They will also waste away because of the guilt of their ancestors.
They will confess their guilt and the guilt of their ancestors—the wrong they committed against me and their hostile conduct toward me.
I too will deal with them in hostility and bring them into the land of their enemies. Then their uncircumcised hearts will be humbled, and then they will accept the punishment for their guilt.
I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham. I will also remember the land.

The land will be abandoned by them and will enjoy its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them. They will accept the punishment for their guilt, because they rejected my judgments and detested my commandments.
Yet even when they were in the land of their enemies, I did not reject them or cast them away. I did not destroy them or break my covenant with them.

Instead, I remembered for their sake the covenant with their ancestors, because I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations and became their God. I am the LORD.
These are the commandments, laws, and judgments that the LORD established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
The LORD spoke with Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When someone makes a special vow to the LORD based on the assessed value of persons,
the assessed value of a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.
If it is a female, her assessed value shall be thirty shekels.
If the person is from five years old up to twenty years old, the assessed value of a male shall be twenty shekels, and that of a female ten shekels.
If the person is from one month old up to five years old, the assessed value of a male shall be five shekels of silver, and that of a female three shekels of silver.
If it is a male sixty years old or older, his assessed value shall be fifteen shekels, and that of a female ten shekels.

If he is too poor to pay the valuation, they shall bring him before the priest, and the priest shall set his value. The priest shall set his value according to what the person who made the vow can afford.
If it is an animal of a kind offered as an offering to the Lord, whatever he gives to the Lord shall be holy.
He shall not exchange it, a good one for a bad one or a bad one for a good one. If he does exchange one animal for another, both it and its replacement shall be holy to the Lord.
If it is an unclean animal of a kind not offered as an offering to the Lord, they shall bring the animal before the priest.
The priest shall set its value, considering whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets shall stand.
If he redeems it, he shall add one-fifth to its value.
If a man dedicates his house as holy to the Lord, the priest shall set its value, considering whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets shall stand.
If the person who dedicated his house redeems it, he shall add one-fifth of its assessed value in silver, and it shall be his.
If a man dedicates to the Lord part of his inherited field, its value shall be in proportion to the seed needed to sow it: fifty shekels of silver for land sown with a kor of barley.
If he dedicates his field from the year of Jubilee, its full valuation shall stand.
If he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, the priest shall calculate the silver due from him according to the years remaining until the year of Jubilee, and shall deduct it from its valuation.
If the person who consecrated the field redeems it, he shall add one-fifth of its value in silver to its price, and it shall be his.
If he does not redeem the field and sells it to another man, it shall no longer be redeemable.
Instead, when the field is released at the Jubilee, it shall be holy to the Lord, like a field irrevocably devoted to him. It shall become the priest’s inherited property.
If the field a man dedicates to the Lord is one he purchased, rather than a field belonging to his inheritance,
the priest shall calculate its value until the year of Jubilee, and he shall pay its value that day as something holy to the Lord.
In the year of Jubilee, the field shall return to the person from whom he bought it, to whom the land belongs as an inheritance.
All its valuations shall be in shekels. A shekel is twenty gerahs.
But no one shall dedicate a firstborn animal that already belongs to the Lord by being firstborn. Whether it is an ox or a sheep, it belongs to the Lord.
If it is an unclean animal, it shall be redeemed at its assessed value, with one-fifth added to it. If it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at its assessed value.

But nothing that a man irrevocably devotes to the Lord from anything he owns—whether a person, an animal, or a field belonging to his inheritance—shall be sold or redeemed. Everything irrevocably devoted is most holy to the Lord.
No person who has been irrevocably devoted shall be redeemed; that person must be put to death.
Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord and is holy to the Lord.
If a man redeems any of his tithe, he shall add one-fifth to it.
Every tithe of cattle and sheep, from all that pass under the shepherd’s staff, shall be holy to the Lord.

He shall not make distinctions between good and bad, or between bad and good, and he shall not exchange it. If he does exchange it, both it and its replacement shall be holy, and it shall not be redeemed.
These are the commandments that the Lord gave Moses concerning the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
